clue.text: Around six balls from fielding position

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for around, as in c.1900
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled by one bowler

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator explains where a fielder stands relative to a six-ball spell.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover is a cricket fielding position on the off side, roughly square of the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cover point, usually just called cover, is a standard place for a fielder in cricket.

parts.note: to sever is to split or cut apart
the heart, or middle letter, of the word sweet is E

explanation.surface: A tricky romantic break-up caused by a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is read as 'sweet heart': the central letter of 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a severe test is a hard or demanding one.

clue.text: Sees term out for American term

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the two words are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a word is foreign, used by Americans for a school period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes SEMESTER from the letters of SEES and TERM; the answer is the US word for a half-year academic term.
explanation.definitionFit: In American colleges the academic year divides into two halves, each called by this name.

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for absolute, as in degrees absolute on a temperature scale
a swine and a git are both insults for a nasty person
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: An utterly horrible pig wolfed down a milkshake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absolute swine' reads as one insult, but it splits into A (absolute) and GIT (the British insult for an unpleasant person).
explanation.definitionFit: To shake a liquid is to stir it up vigorously, the physical sense of the verb.

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other, so the woods surround the second

parts.note: woods is another word for a forest
a mo, short for moment, is a second, as in wait a mo

explanation.surface: A question about whether the golfer Tiger Woods came first after a second place.
explanation.walkthrough: Woods suggests the golfer, but it is just trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: the foremost person is at the front, ahead of all the rest.

parts.note: to deter someone is to put them off
gent is short for gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: Housework discouraged a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is used here as an adjective, as in a cleansing agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adjectivally, the word describes something with a cleansing action, like soap powder.

clue.text: Independent gives one rubbish about right

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the abbreviation for right
rubbish is read as a verb or adjective of disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A free-thinking person dismisses someone as worthless when talking about what is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' is the anagram signal, making SOVEEIGN, and 'about' puts R (right) inside it; 'gives one' reads as a verb phrase but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign state is self-governing, not ruled by another power.

indicators.note: say tells us the word for plank is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a plank is a board of wood

explanation.surface: A carpenter has made holes through a length of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pronunciation, without a sounded R, BOARD and BORED sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To bore a hole is to drill one, so something drilled has been holed through.

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword abbreviation for the Queen
a go is a turn or move in a game

explanation.surface: A chess player decides the best play is advancing the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture is misleading: queen is ER and move is GO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word is used in English as a logical connective meaning consequently.

clue.text: Strong, strong guys held in check

indicators.note: held in means the muscular men are contained within the word for check

parts.note: to vet something is to check or examine it
he-men are muscular, macho men

explanation.surface: Powerful bodybuilders are kept under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strong' appears twice: first as the definition, then as part of the phrase for he-men.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: vehement feelings are intense, forceful or passionate.

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for the drug sits inside the verb for pass on

parts.note: to refer a matter is to pass it on to someone else
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug user declines a pill while smoking.
explanation.walkthrough: Pass on looks like refuse, but here it means hand over to someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is slang for a cannabis cigarette, also called a joint.

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A question about a man who works on a well-known American news weekly.
explanation.walkthrough: Time is a famous magazine, which misleads; but the answer is a different magazine: Heat is a British celebrity gossip weekly.
explanation.definitionFit: Heat is the title of a popular British celebrity weekly.

parts.note: tho is the informal, everyday spelling of though, meaning even if
coarse means rough to the touch

explanation.surface: Something ideal, even if it is ordinary and crude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' signals the informal shortening THO.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an intensifier, as in a complete or utter nuisance, the word means absolute or perfect.

clue.text: Yacht is able to, circling a river

indicators.note: circling means the word for is able to goes round the letters that follow

parts.note: can means is able to
the Tamar is a river in south-west England, between Devon and Cornwall

explanation.surface: A sailing boat manages to go around a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar is a river forming most of the Devon-Cornwall border in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a twin-hulled sailing boat, a kind of yacht.

parts.note: Eminem is a rapper, so his music is rap
a port is an opening, as in a porthole or a computer port

explanation.surface: A rapper's music starts out with harmony.
explanation.walkthrough: Opening looks like a start, but it is PORT, a hole or gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, sympathetic relationship, the kind of harmony between people who get along.

indicators.note: found in means the insect is placed within the word for common

parts.note: plain means ordinary or common
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug is discovered on an everyday garden weed.
explanation.walkthrough: Plantain here is the common garden weed of the genus Plantago, not the banana-like fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The genus Plantago includes many wild plants regarded by gardeners as lawn pests.

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A musician plays a flattened note that dissolves things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' rearranges NOTE to make TONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a common chemical solvent, used in nail varnish remover.

clue.text: Case of caviar, palatable, easy to swallow

indicators.note: case of means the outside letters of caviar, its first and last letters

parts.note: palatable food is edible, fit to eat

explanation.surface: A tin of fish eggs proves tasty and easy to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'easy to swallow' seems to be about food, but it means believable.
explanation.definitionFit: A credible story is believable, something a listener readily accepts.

clue.text: Right admitting head of state's boom

indicators.note: admitting means the word for right lets in the letter that follows

parts.note: proper means right or correct

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word state

explanation.surface: A political right wing embraces a nation's leader during an economic boom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boom' is the verb: to thrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To boom is to thrive, as a growing economy does.

clue.text: Drunken dare with a rum raider

indicators.note: drunken suggests the letters stagger about into a new order

explanation.surface: A pirate gets drunk on rum after a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' rearranges DARE, A and RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A marauder roams about attacking and plundering, as a raider does.

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as in family trees
art can mean cunning or artfulness, as in artful

explanation.surface: A quick glimpse reveals someone deceased and very sly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' is the verb: to move very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to move suddenly and quickly, as a bird or fish does.

clue.text: Journalist, for example, back on side

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is a common crossword journalist

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation for for example is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A reporter, for instance, returns to work on the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses EG to give GE.
explanation.definitionFit: The edge of something is its border or side.

parts.note: a range is a spread, as in a spread of options

explanation.surface: A fine meal is laid out at a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' suggests a feast but means a range.
explanation.definitionFit: A grange is a country house, often one with farm buildings.

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Conservative

parts.note: to lash is to whip, so the whip's is the lash

explanation.surface: Tory leader and the party whip are in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Parliament, a whip enforces party discipline; here whip is just LASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a clash is a fight or conflict.

clue.text: Constituent in favour of accepting law

indicators.note: accepting means the word for in favour of takes in the word for law

parts.note: being for something means being in favour of it
an act of parliament is a law

explanation.surface: A voter in a constituency supports a new piece of legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constituent' suggests a voter, but it means a component.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a factor is one of the elements or ingredients that make up something.

indicators.note: wrong means set out incorrectly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Even if we are mistaken, we are still deserving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges US and ALBEIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worthy is suitable, as in fit or deserving of a role.

indicators.note: inside signals that the answer runs through the words semiconductor and a diode

explanation.surface: Asks whether electronic parts are found within this device.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: radios contain semiconductor components such as diodes.
explanation.definitionFit: A transistor set contains diodes and other semiconductors.

clue.text: Some lingo translated for new expression

indicators.note: translated means the letters are converted into another form

explanation.surface: Part of a language is rendered into a fresh phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges SOME LINGO.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly coined word or phrase.
